input.brief: Sooth: a stop-loss for native DOGE that sells from your own wallet only when a signed price crosses your stop, always leaving DOGE for gas

direction.name: The printed annual
direction.idea: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.
direction.composition: A fixed vertical axis at about 42% of the viewport width organises everything: headings begin on it, body columns hang from it, and the 0–42% zone holds small side notes, figures or stays empty. Masthead: a wide image band (photographic mosaic or a single crop) across the top 45% of the first screen; below it the title at 7–9vw starting on the axis, with a two-sentence standfirst at 20–24px. Sections alternate between text pages (title on the axis, body in one or two columns of 34–40ch to its right) and full-bleed colour pages carrying one large figure, quotation or image mosaic. Mosaics are gutterless: photographs and flat colour tiles butted together in a 4- or 6-cell grid. Page numbers, running heads and other print furniture are left out.
direction.typography: A tight heavy grotesk or a sharp serif for titles; an excellent text face for reading at 18–20px with leading near 1.5. Headings in sentence case, tracked tight.
direction.colour: Paper, ink and two or three solid block colours. A colour page is a whole section in one flat colour.
direction.imagery: Photographs used as blocks in mosaics alongside flat colour tiles; mixed subjects are fine if cropped tight and converted to one treatment.
direction.photoTreatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.
direction.richness: The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.
direction.pitfalls: The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

hero.name: View with two cards in the corner
hero.blueprint: One photograph or muted film fills the viewport, `object-fit: cover`, with the subject in the right half. The headline sits on the left at mid-height: two lines at clamp(44px, 3.9vw, 60px), bold, leading 1.08, flush to the 32px margin on columns 1–5, the block vertically centred; 20px below it, one supporting sentence at 18px, max 40ch, in the paper colour. In the bottom-right corner, 32px from the right and bottom edges, two cards sit side by side with a 16px gap, each two columns wide (about 210px) at 3:2: a photograph of the newest thing (a project, an edition, an article) with a paper-colour bar 40px tall fused to its lower edge, holding its title at 16px on the left and a small arrow on the right. They are the next steps after the single action, which is a solid rectangle top-right beside a menu word. One short fact at 16px in the paper colour may be pinned onto the subject itself, beside a solid 8px dot on the point it describes, with no line joining them. Wordmark top-left on the 32px margin. If the left half is light, lay a neutral dark scrim under columns 1–6 only.
hero.mobile: The picture is re-cropped to portrait with the subject in the upper half. The headline sits at 9vw on two lines on the 16px margin at 44% of the height, with the sentence at 16px beneath it. The two cards sit side by side across the full width at the bottom, 16px from the edges, each about 171px wide at 3:2 with its title bar. Wordmark top-left; the action and a menu word top-right.
hero.headline: A plain two-line claim of 4–7 words, at most about 17 characters per line at 3.9vw.

type.name: Hanken Grotesk

display.settings: weight 500 · tracking -0.05em · leading 0.9 · sentence case; one statement size (about 6vw) used for every heading

type.note: Medium-weight grotesk statements at one large size against caption-size text: a two-size system with no bold. Suits portfolios, agencies and tools that speak in short declarative lines.

palette.name: Oxblood and grey
palette.note: Deep red text on grey paper holds most of the page, then pale grey text on a solid red field takes one long section and the footer. Photographs are desaturated so nothing breaks the pair, and the button is a solid red block.

photos.title: Sky and space
photos.note: skies, clouds, stars and night skies
photos.treatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.

photos.alt: A few birds flying across a pale blue gradient sky
Tiny aeroplane crossing a wide, softly overcast sky
Green aurora sweeping across the night sky above snowy ground
Tiny silhouetted figure on a dark ridge under a blue and orange twilight sky

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Lead line over four columns
sections.blueprint: Two parts on one 12-column grid with 20px margins. First, a lead paragraph of 30–40 words spans all 12 columns at clamp(22px, 2.2vw, 32px), regular weight, leading 1.2: three lines that read as the opening of a text, with no heading before it. 72px below, four equal columns (three grid columns each, 24px gutters) carry small text at 14–15px with leading 1.45. Each column is one paragraph of 40–70 words that opens with a bold run-in phrase of two or three words in full ink, the rest continuing on the same line in the soft ink. Columns top-align and end ragged at different depths. No cards, icons or dividers; the bold run-ins are the only markers. The four columns answer four plain questions: who, what, where, how to reach them. Padding is modest, 96px top and bottom, so a sheet of images can start straight after.
sections.mobile: The lead paragraph at 20px, full width. The four columns become a two-by-two grid with a 20px gutter and 40px row gap at 14px; if any paragraph exceeds 60 words, switch to one column with 32px between paragraphs. Run-in phrases stay bold.

sections.name: Call and response column
sections.blueprint: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

sections.name: Fixed output, live controls
sections.blueprint: A split the reader operates. Left, columns 1–6: a flat colour field that is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh, edge to edge, holding one thing the product makes (a card, an email, a chart, a rendered page) centred at true size, about 420px wide, root marked data-ui. Right, columns 8–12: a reading column no wider than 44ch, with four or five capability blocks 50vh apart. Each block is a sentence at 28–32px, a paragraph at 17px, and directly beneath it one real control at interface size: a slider, a segmented choice, a toggle, a short text field. Operating a control changes the fixed output on the left at once, and changes persist, so by the last block the reader has configured their own. The section heading, two to four words at 40–44px, opens the right column, 72px from the top.
sections.mobile: The output sits in a sticky field at the top, 42svh tall, cropped to its most telling region, not shrunk. Blocks scroll beneath on the page ground: sentence at 22px, paragraph at 16px, control at full width with 44px targets. The field releases after the last block.

sections.name: Plain names in columns
sections.blueprint: A typographic list with no logos. The heading, two or three words at 28–32px, sits in columns 1–3 and stays top-aligned with the first row of names. Columns 5–12 hold the names in three or four text columns (`columns: 4; column-gap: 32px`), each name on its own line at 20–22px with leading 1.5, sentence case, in the full ink. Where names fall into kinds (clients, press, partners), each kind starts a new column and its first line names the kind in the softer ink at the same size, so no small labels are needed. Columns are of unequal length and are not balanced; ragged bottoms are intended. Twelve to thirty names work best. There are no boxes, bullets or separators: the column edges and the shared baseline do the organising. Leave 120px above and below.
sections.mobile: The heading leads at 26px. Names follow in two columns at 17px with a 20px gap; each kind begins after a 32px break with its name in the softer ink on the first line. Long names wrap inside their column rather than shrinking.

sections.name: Cards that fold into spines
sections.blueprint: For a journal, a run of notes or a list of chapters without pictures. A wrapper about 400svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. The heading, two to four words at clamp(48px, 4.2vw, 64px), sits top-left on the 32px margin, 120px from the top. Under it a band 360px tall spans the content width and holds a horizontal deck of text cards, each about 620px wide, in three neighbouring flat tones of one hue taken in turn. On a card, with 32px padding: its title at 30px on up to two lines, leading 1.1; an excerpt of two lines at 16px; and along the bottom edge the date on the left and a text link to read it on the right, both at 16px. As the page scrolls, each step slides the next card in from the right edge and squeezes the earlier ones into slivers 120px wide stacked edge to edge at the left, like book spines, where only the first letters of their titles show, clipped by the sliver. Clicking a sliver brings its card back. 48px under the band, the number of entries and a link to the full list sit at 17px on the left margin, so the stage does not end on an empty floor.
sections.mobile: No pin and no slivers. The cards stack at full width with 12px gaps, each in its tone, the title at 24px, the excerpt at 16px, the date and link at the foot. The heading sits above them at 10vw.

sections.name: The idea again, inverted
sections.blueprint: The close flips the page's colours: ink becomes the ground and the ground becomes the ink, across a full-bleed field at least 90svh tall. The page's opening idea returns as a headline of three to five words at 9–11vw on two lines, leading 0.9, flush left, positioned in the upper two-thirds; it should echo the hero's wording, not repeat it. Along the bottom, on one shared baseline 40px above the edge: one supporting sentence at 20px in columns 1–5 and one rectangular button in the accent colour, right-aligned in columns 10–12, about 56px tall. Nothing else: no image, no second button, no logo. The field's top edge is a hard horizontal line where it meets the section above. If the footer follows on the same inverted field, leave 160px before it so the close still reads as its own screen.
sections.mobile: The same inverted field at 80svh. Headline at 15vw on two lines at the top. The sentence sits lower at 17px, and the button spans the full width at the bottom, 56px tall, with 20px margins. Nothing else is added.

sections.name: Columns above, wordmark below
sections.blueprint: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
sections.mobile: Columns become two by two at 15px with 32px between rows, at the top. A gap of about 20svh follows. The wordmark spans the full width at the bottom; a name longer than ten letters stacks on two lines, each fitted to the width. Legal line beneath at 12px.

references.name: Architecture of Socialist-Era Belgrade
references.idea: A two-colour printed guidebook on screen: signal-red type over greyscale concrete, with one modular display face as the only ornament.
references.hero: Full-bleed greyscale photograph of brutalist housing towers; pale sky fills the top half, concrete the bottom. The title is set over the sky, flush left at a 32px margin, three lines in a wide modular display face at 102px (7.1vw) in flat red, the longest line reaching 92% of the width, leading so tight that the lines almost touch. Under it, one row at 24px: a red one-line descriptor at left, and two paler-red facts right-aligned (an object count and a date range). Top-right, the word 'Index' with a diagonal arrow. No logo, no button, nothing else. Red and grey only.
references.type: IntraNet, a wide modular display face with rounded, notched corners, used only for the title and its footer repeat. Funnel Sans carries the rest: about 50px for the long intro, 40px bold uppercase entry titles, 24px meta, 13px credits. Four sizes, two faces.
references.colour: #f53843 #d1d1d1 #c7c7c7 #777777 #f1a7ab — Strictly red and grey: red text on grey photo or grey paper, then pale grey text on a solid red field for the essay and footer. Photographs are desaturated so nothing breaks the pair.
references.imagery: Contemporary black-and-white architectural photographs of concrete towers and complexes, frontal or looking up, with big skies and visible grain; full-bleed in the hero, full column width and square-cornered in entries.
references.layout: 16 to 32px margins, everything flush left. A long red essay block in very large text, then twenty repeated entry blocks on grey: a two-column header split by a vertical red hairline, a meta row, then a wide photo. 81 screens of the same rhythm.

sections.description: Immediately under the hero photo a solid red field begins with no gap. The essay runs as one full-width column in pale grey sans at roughly 50px with tight leading, about 50 characters per line, paragraphs separated by one blank line, with no headings, pull-quotes or images for several screens. The photo's bottom edge butts straight against the red.

Each building entry sits on light grey paper: a thin red rule across the top, then two columns divided by a vertical red hairline at the 50% mark. Left: the building's name in red bold uppercase at 40px over two lines. Right: its dates in pale red at the same size. Below, a small meta row with 'Credits' and 'Address' labels and values in 13px red, then a full-width greyscale photograph.

Solid red. At the top, two short 13px notes side by side in pale grey occupy the left 60%, a back-to-top link sits far right, and a third note runs beneath. A tall empty red gap follows. Then the full title is repeated in the display face at hero size but in pale grey, flush left, above a single row of small meta: sources link left, font credits centre, city and year right.

steal: Limit the page to one saturated colour and one grey, desaturate all photos, and invert the pair (grey on red) for long reading blocks.
Set the title in a distinctive modular display face directly on the sky area of a photo and repeat it in the footer in the inverse colour.
Put facts in the hero as a right-aligned row of paler-tint figures (count, date range) on the same baseline as the subtitle.

references.name: Artem Taradash
references.idea: A designer's CV compressed into one newspaper-like band at the top, after which oversized product renders and project artefacts speak at full scale.
references.hero: White page with 20px margins. Top-left are three small black rectangular tags with white text (name and two links). Below them a three-line statement at about 3vw in regular-weight grotesk fills the first third, left-aligned. To its right, starting at the very top edge, run two narrow columns of 12px text, then a third column listing clients one per line, and in the far top-right a circular portrait about 200px wide with a white hand-lettered word across the face. This text band ends by a quarter of the height. Below it a huge cut-out vehicle render bleeds off the bottom, with a project card at right.
references.type: One family, Diatype, in regular weight throughout. Three sizes: about 43px for statements and project titles, 12.4px for all running text, about 11px for tags. Tight leading, sentence case, no bold and no capitals; hierarchy comes from size alone.
references.colour: #ffffff #111111 #f7f9fb #1c4fd8 #f0a23a — Strictly black on white for the frame. All colour arrives with project material: an orange-to-blue gradient, a cobalt zigzag pattern, warm photography.
references.imagery: Product renders cut out on white and shown very large, interface screenshots with a small corner radius, a full-width studio photo with a circular logo overlaid, and textile-pattern fields running margin to margin. Scale varies sharply between projects.
references.layout: A loose six-column grid with 20px margins; small text blocks hang from column lines beside very large images. Each project is arranged differently, and there are no dividers or section backgrounds, only white space and jumps in scale. The tag nav stays fixed top-left.

sections.description: Each project pairs one oversized visual with a small caption cluster. In the first, a cut-out product render fills the left 60% and bleeds off the edge. The right third stacks a landscape screenshot with slightly rounded corners, then a row holding a tiny label and two-line title at about 3vw on the left and a five-line 12px description on the right.

A row of three: a round black watch-face mock-up about a quarter of the width, a wide rectangle filled with a horizontal blue, violet, orange, blue gradient with a tiny tick scale beneath it, and a narrow text column at far right with label, three-line title and two short paragraphs. Circle, rectangle and text share a top line.

A cobalt-and-white zigzag textile pattern runs margin to margin for more than a full viewport height with only a two-line caption beneath it at left. Before it, a black-backed mosaic of pattern samples and report-cover mock-ups sits beside two narrow text columns. The pattern is given a section to itself with no mock-up frame.

Closing row on white: a tiny label, then a four-line sentence at about 3vw in the left third; a small square portrait at the two-thirds mark; to its right a short question with two underlined links below. All three hang from the same top line with empty space between them.

steal: Put bio, client list and portrait in one compact multi-column band at the top so the first scroll is already work.
Use solid black rectangular tags with white text as the only navigation chrome.
Let one project artefact (a pattern, a gradient) run full width for a whole screen with a two-line caption instead of framing it in a mock-up.

references.name: UGLYCASH
references.idea: A money app sold like streetwear: one shouted condensed headline over the phone, then sticker-covered 3D props where feature icons would normally go.
references.hero: Near-white page. A floating light-grey nav bar only 35% of the viewport wide sits centred 20px from the top: condensed wordmark left, two social icons in the middle, an app button with a glowing magenta outline right. Directly beneath, a two-line uppercase headline in bold condensed grotesque at 11.4vw, centred, leading under 0.9, about 60% of the width, with a faint cyan and magenta fringe on the letter edges; it fills the band from 12% to 43% of the height. A single phone mockup 27% of the viewport wide rises immediately under the headline, centred, cut off by the bottom edge. Its magenta screen glow is the only colour.
references.type: Helvetica Now Display Condensed Bold in capitals at 164px with -0.033em tracking and very tight leading; the same face in mixed case near 34px for section headings. Inter at 14px, semi-bold, for captions. Two faces and a roughly 12:1 jump.
references.colour: #f7f7f7 #000000 #ffffff #ff00e6 #b6ff00 #00aeef — Off-white ground, white cards, black type. Neon magenta, lime and cyan appear only as whole-card fills, glows and stickers, never in text. Cool and synthetic overall.
references.imagery: Phone mockups with real app screens, plus glossy 3D props (money bags, a holographic card, an eagle, a wet-floor sign, banknotes) covered in die-cut stickers, each centred in a rounded card; some cards have grainy neon gradients.
references.layout: Content sits in a centred column about 60% of the viewport wide. Sections open with a left-aligned condensed heading, then rows of two or three rounded cards with captions placed outside and below. A horizontal carousel and a centred uppercase statement break the rhythm.

sections.description: A left-aligned two-line condensed heading near 34px above a row of three equal cards with 8px gaps and small radius: one pale grey with a cropped balance readout and tilted stickers, one white with two 3D money bags, one solid cyan with a phone cropped at the bottom. Captions sit beneath each card rather than inside: a bold one-word title and two short 13px lines.

Two near-square cards side by side, each half the column. Left: a grainy lime-to-lilac gradient with a white floating panel listing three rows, each with a flag, a label and a small pill button. Right: a white card with a black holographic payment card tilted about 25 degrees, stickers stuck to it. A later pair repeats the pattern with a solid magenta card holding a white icon-grid panel.

Trust carousel: a horizontal row of tall cards, each showing one 3D object centred (a chrome eagle on white, a banknote on solid lime, a yellow wet-floor sign with hand-lettered warning). The title sits inside the first card and below the others. A tiny two-dot pager is centred underneath and the next card peeks in orange at the right edge of the column.

A white rounded panel the width of the column in which the wordmark is scaled to fill the panel edge to edge, about 55% of the viewport, in black ultra-condensed capitals. Beneath it, one row with a small parent-brand credit at left and two store badges at right, then legal small print in 11px at left and four right-aligned links.

steal: Make the nav a short floating bar a third of the viewport wide so the headline can start almost at the top edge.
Replace feature icons with one photoreal 3D prop per card, each covered in die-cut stickers, and keep captions outside the card.
End with the wordmark scaled to exactly fill a white footer card, with all legal text beneath it at 11px.
